context: Found while finishing batch corpus-rule-r4 on 2026-11-27.
description:
## Problem
Finishing the members of batch corpus-rule-r4 (PR #4521, merged 2026-11-27) was refused with `final evidence changed_files drifted from the registered integration tree`. The two tools exclude develop-merge files differently:
- The tracker server (tractable 1.3.2, `store.excluded_paths`, checked in `service._validate_final_checkout`) excludes every file listed by a develop-merge entry of the integration log unless a member receipt or a fix entry also lists it.
- BenchBox's evidence script (`scripts/batch_integration.py` `build_evidence` via `pr_landing.develop_exclusions`) excludes a develop-merge file only when the final tree matches the merged develop parent for it, so a develop merge cannot hide branch changes.

The batch's first develop merge (91f817fc87, recorded 2026-11-23) carried this PR's own edits to tests/unit/scripts/test_generate_standard_scales.py and docs/internal/dev-loop-property-ledger.md through conflict resolution. The script listed them (189 files); the server expected them excluded (187). The owner chose to finish with the server's set and record the two files (crr-00 context, 2026-11-27). The server now refuses such merges up front ('merge introduces non-develop content'), but evidence for a batch that predates that check can still disagree.

## Change
- Decide which rule is authoritative and make both tools use it. The stricter rule (a develop-merge file stays in scope when the branch differs from develop) is the one that cannot hide branch content; adopting it on the server needs a tractable change, released and pinned.
- Until then, make build_evidence report any file it keeps that the server will exclude (or the reverse), naming the file and the develop merge, before the leader calls finish.

## Decision gates
- Changing the server's rule is the owner's decision (it ships in the pinned tractable release); present both options with their effect on past batches.
- Never weaken the script's rule to match the server without the owner's approval.

## Verification rubric
- A test builds a batch whose develop merge carries a branch edit and shows both tools produce the same changed_files, or the script reports the difference before finish.

## Guardrails
- Reproduce or measure before changing anything; record the command, log path and run id in the item context.
- Fix the root cause. Never skip, xfail, loosen a check or bound, or raise a timeout only to make a test or run pass; a timing or limit change needs measured evidence and owner approval.
- No rule, check, label or test may name a platform or a version matrix unless the item is about that platform.
- Never edit stored result files under results-data/ or CHANGELOG.md; user-facing changes add a changelog.d fragment.
- No explanatory comments or docstrings (make comment-policy-check); make duplicate-check-delta stays at +0; reuse existing helpers.
- Heavy work only through make heavy-run after make heavy-status, with command, maximum run time and log path announced first. Never touch the lock or set BENCHBOX_SKIP_TEST_LOCK, BENCHBOX_HEAVY_ADMIT=force, BENCHBOX_HEAVY_WATCHDOG=off, or raise BENCHBOX_HEAVY_MEMORY_BUDGET_GIB. No live cloud runs.
- Work in a linked worktree; one pull request; run the local review before opening it; fix hosted-review findings. No stand-in approval unless the owner names the PR and head.
- Re-read paths and line numbers before editing and report drift instead of guessing.
- When a decision gate's stop condition is met, stop and report to the owner with the evidence; never substitute a different decision.
